chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Bazowari said: Humayd ibn Ziyad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a free woman and found her to be a slave girl who had concealed her status: He (peace be upon him) said, 'If the one who married her to him was not her masters, then his marriage is invalid.' I asked, 'What should he do with the dowry she took from him?' He said, 'If he finds something of what he gave her, let him take it; and if he does not find anything, she has nothing due to him. If the one who married her was her guardian, he shall seek recourse against her guardian for what she took, and against her masters. If she was a virgin, one-tenth of her price is due to the masters; and if she was not a virgin, half of one-tenth of her price is due, for what he made lawful of her private part.' He said, 'And she observes the waiting period of a slave girl.' I asked, 'If she brings forth a child from him?' He said, 'The children are free, if the marriage was without the master's permission.' And we have discussed this report previously and clarified the meaning of his saying 'The children are free,' i.e., what is meant by it, so there is no need to repeat it here. Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever proposed to a man for his daughter from a free woman, but he contracted marriage for her with his daughter from a slave girl, and then he learned of that afterwards, he has the right to return her.'

key_terms.عِدَّةَ ٱلْأَمَةِ: Waiting period of a slave girl

ai.seo_question: What are the fiqh rulings when a man marries a free woman who turns out to be a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *tadlis* (concealment of status) in marriage, specifically addressing the validity of unions when a free woman is mistaken for a slave or vice versa. It details the financial liabilities, including the return of the dowry and compensation to the master based on virginity, while clarifying that offspring remain free if the master did not consent to the marriage. The text also notes the specific waiting period (*iddah*) applicable to the slave woman, reflecting the practical legal concerns of the Shia scholarly tradition regarding property rights and lineage.
